title: Activation spec: onboarding email sequence
text: # Activation spec: onboarding email sequence Owner: Mira Venn, Product. Scope: automated messages sent to new Pulse workspace administrators, not the in-app onboarding checklist. ## Problem and outcome New administrators create a workspace but often leave before importing an audience. This specification proposes three lifecycle emails: a welcome message immediately after verification, an import guide after twenty-four hours without an import, and a campaign-building guide after the first successful import. These are Pulse product messages, not campaigns customers send to their own subscribers. ## Decisions D-01: We chose behavior-triggered onboarding emails instead of a fixed daily sequence because completed actions should suppress irrelevant instructions. A completed import cancels the pending import guide. D-02: We limited the sequence to verified workspace administrators because collaborators without setup permissions cannot complete the requested tasks. This is an initial scope restriction, not a deliverability requirement.

D-02: We limited the sequence to verified workspace administrators because collaborators without setup permissions cannot complete the requested tasks. This is an initial scope restriction, not a deliverability requirement. ## Acceptance criteria Each message contains one primary action, a preference-management link, and the workspace name. No subscriber addresses appear in these emails. An administrator who belongs to two workspaces receives independently evaluated messages, capped at one onboarding email per day across both workspaces. An email delivery event does not mark an in-app checklist task complete. The checklist reads actual workspace actions and has its own acceptance rules in DOC-002. ## Measurement and open questions Measure verified administrators reaching their first sent campaign within seven days. Track unsubscribe rate separately from activation so increased messaging cannot hide dissatisfaction. D-02 will be reviewed after collaborator interviews; no expansion is approved in this document. Delivery implementation and suppression tests belong to TCK-001.

title: Activation spec: in-app onboarding checklist
text: # Activation spec: in-app onboarding checklist Owner: Elian Marr, Design. Scope: the persistent setup panel inside Pulse, not the onboarding email sequence described in DOC-001. ## Experience The panel contains three tasks: verify a sending domain, import an audience, and create a draft campaign. Each task links to the relevant screen. Creating a draft completes the third task even if the campaign is never sent; the panel represents setup progress rather than the activation metric used by the lifecycle-email project. ## Decisions D-03: We made the checklist dismissible because experienced administrators should not have a permanent setup panel after migrating from another tool. Dismissing it is a per-user preference and does not change workspace task state. D-04: We derive completion from persisted workspace events because a clicked help link does not prove that a setup action succeeded. Failed imports leave the import task incomplete.

title: Activation spec: in-app onboarding checklist
text: it is a per-user preference and does not change workspace task state. D-04: We derive completion from persisted workspace events because a clicked help link does not prove that a setup action succeeded. Failed imports leave the import task incomplete. ## Permissions and boundaries Administrators can perform all three tasks. Collaborators see the same workspace progress but receive a permission explanation instead of an unavailable action. Reading a guide, opening an onboarding email, or receiving an email delivery notification never completes a task. Checklist state must survive refreshes and support two administrators working simultaneously. A removed verified domain reopens the verification task. Existing campaign drafts count when the panel is introduced. ## Validation TCK-002 covers dismissal persistence and task-state tests. CHAT-001 records confusion between email suppression and checklist completion. Usability sessions will ask participants to explain why a task is complete; success means they cite the underlying action rather than a message they received. No additional lifecycle emails are authorized by this specification.

title: Roadmap decision: subscriber CSV export postponed
text: # Roadmap decision: subscriber CSV export postponed Owner: Sora Pell, Engineering. This record concerns downloading subscriber records from a workspace. It does not cover campaign performance reports, chart images, or inbound CSV imports. ## Decision and reason D-05: We postponed subscriber CSV export from the spring milestone because the existing read path does not reliably apply field-level access restrictions to custom attributes. Shipping a download before enforcing those restrictions could expose fields a collaborator cannot view in the interface. The feature is postponed, not cancelled. There is no committed release date. TCK-003 remains blocked until an authorization design and test matrix are reviewed. Support must not promise a release based on the existence of the ticket. ## Scope of a future implementation A subscriber export would include email address, subscription state, and authorized custom fields for a selected audience. Suppression reasons need separate review. Downloads would require an administrator, an expiring link, and an audit event. These are proposed requirements, not delivered capabilities.

D-06: We kept campaign report PDF work in the current milestone because its aggregate metrics do not depend on the restricted subscriber-field read path. A PDF report must not include recipient-level rows or subscriber addresses. ## Communication and review The roadmap should use the label “subscriber CSV export: postponed, authorization dependency.” Avoid the unqualified phrase “exports postponed,” which could incorrectly imply that aggregate campaign reporting is also blocked. Review D-05 after the authorization prototype passes negative-permission tests. A working prototype alone does not authorize a public launch.

title: Deliverability decision: shared suppression list baseline
text: # Deliverability decision: shared suppression list baseline Owner: Neri Vale, Messaging Infrastructure. This record defines the initial scope of suppression caused by a recipient unsubscribe. It does not define whether an administrator receives Pulse onboarding emails. ## Initial policy D-07: We chose workspace-wide unsubscribe suppression because the initial sender identity model provides only one recognizable brand per workspace. A recipient who unsubscribes should not receive another campaign merely because the sender selected a different audience. A matching normalized address is suppressed across audiences within that workspace. An unsubscribe in one workspace does not change another workspace. Hard-bounce handling is a separate mechanism and remains workspace-wide under this proposal. ## Implementation contract The send worker checks suppression immediately before delivery, not only when assembling a campaign audience. The preferences page explains the affected workspace. Audit records retain the event type, timestamp, and initiating campaign identifier, without copying the entire message body. TCK-005 implements the initial unsubscribe scope. It must include a test in which a recipient belongs to two audiences and unsubscribes through a campaign sent to only one of them.

title: Deliverability decision: shared suppression list baseline

It must include a test in which a recipient belongs to two audiences and unsubscribes through a campaign sent to only one of them. ## Limitations and review The policy may be too broad for customers operating distinct publications under one workspace. For this initial version, the interface must explicitly describe the workspace-wide effect; it must not claim that an unsubscribe is limited to one audience. A later policy change requires a dated replacement record and an explicit rule for existing suppressions. Customer feedback can motivate that review but cannot silently alter the worker contract. CHAT-004 will be used to collect publication-specific feedback after the initial implementation is tested.

title: Decision update: publication-scoped unsubscribe policy
text: # Decision update: publication-scoped unsubscribe policy Owner: Neri Vale, Messaging Infrastructure. This record supersedes D-07 in DOC-004 for unsubscribe events created after the new policy is enabled. It does not reverse the subscriber-export postponement in DOC-003. ## Updated decision D-12: We replaced workspace-wide unsubscribe suppression for new unsubscribe events with publication-scoped suppression because pilot feedback showed that recipients recognized separate publications and wanted to leave one without leaving all of them. CHAT-004 documents the feedback; TCK-005 records the implementation update. A publication is a named sending stream with its own recipient-facing identity. It is not an audience or a saved segment. Each campaign must select exactly one publication before scheduling. Membership in overlapping audiences does not broaden the unsubscribe scope. ## Safety and migration D-13: We preserved existing workspace-wide unsubscribe records because narrowing an earlier opt-out without new permission could restart messages recipients expected to stop. The migration does not infer publication consent from opens, clicks, or audience membership.

title: Decision update: publication-scoped unsubscribe policy

title: Audience import preview and recoverable validation
text: # Audience import preview and recoverable validation Owner: Tavin Reed. Scope: a one-time CSV upload into a selected Pulse audience. This workflow does not maintain an ongoing connection to another system and does not download existing subscribers. ## Product contract The administrator maps columns, previews validation results, and confirms accepted rows before any audience membership changes. A preview reports invalid addresses and missing required values without displaying unrelated workspace records. Uploading a file alone does not complete the import task in DOC-002; a successfully committed import does. ## Decisions D-15: We chose partial acceptance with an explicit preview because one malformed row should not force administrators to repair an otherwise usable file before understanding the problem. Confirmation shows accepted and rejected counts separately. D-16: We postponed downloadable rejected-row files because the existing field-authorization gap could expose submitted custom attributes through a second download path. The first version provides an authenticated on-screen error summary instead. This does not change D-05, which postpones subscriber CSV export.

title: Audience import preview and recoverable validation
text: We postponed downloadable rejected-row files because the existing field-authorization gap could expose submitted custom attributes through a second download path. The first version provides an authenticated on-screen error summary instead. This does not change D-05, which postpones subscriber CSV export. ## Acceptance and boundaries A confirmed import must not revive any suppressed address. Duplicate normalized addresses update permitted fields under a documented merge rule and count separately from newly created subscribers. Retrying the same confirmation must not create duplicate memberships. TCK-006 owns the preview implementation. Ongoing subscriber synchronization belongs to DOC-007 and must not be described as an automated version of this upload without specifying conflict behavior. A later decision is required before downloadable rejection artifacts can enter scope.

title: Subscriber sync connector baseline and conflict policy
text: # Subscriber sync connector baseline and conflict policy Owner: Sora Pell. Scope: recurring inbound subscriber updates from a fictional customer-managed source. This is not the one-time audience CSV import in DOC-006 and does not provide outbound subscriber export. ## Product contract An administrator configures one source identifier and a target audience. A sync run records its start time, completion state, and aggregate counts. Missing source records do not delete Pulse subscribers automatically. Suppression checks remain authoritative regardless of source values. ## Decisions D-17: We chose nightly batch synchronization rather than an on-demand refresh because the first worker design lacks a safe per-source concurrency guard and overlapping runs could apply updates out of order. This is an initial scheduling policy, not a permanent product limitation. D-18: We made Pulse suppression state authoritative because an upstream subscribed flag must not silently undo a recipient's unsubscribe. Source updates may change permitted profile fields but cannot clear an opt-out.

title: Subscriber sync connector baseline and conflict policy
text: an initial scheduling policy, not a permanent product limitation. D-18: We made Pulse suppression state authoritative because an upstream subscribed flag must not silently undo a recipient's unsubscribe. Source updates may change permitted profile fields but cannot clear an opt-out. ## Conflict handling The connector records a source revision for every accepted update. An older revision must not overwrite a newer one. Source failures leave the last successful state visible and do not mark the audience empty. Administrators see a summary rather than a downloadable subscriber-level reconciliation file. TCK-007 implements this baseline. DOC-006 remains the contract for manual uploads; its partial-acceptance preview does not establish synchronization scheduling. Any later addition of manual refresh requires a replacement decision explaining serialization and duplicate-request handling. Neither this connector nor its status screen resolves the export authorization dependency in DOC-003.

title: Bounce classification and retry boundaries
text: # Bounce classification and retry boundaries Owner: Neri Vale. Scope: delivery failures reported by the sending transport. A bounce is not a recipient unsubscribe, and classifying a transport response must not create publication consent. ## Classification contract Persist an event identifier, campaign identifier, response category, and receipt timestamp. A definitive permanent delivery failure is a hard bounce. A temporary failure is a soft bounce and can remain eligible for bounded retries. Unknown responses remain unclassified pending review instead of being treated as consent changes. ## Decisions D-19: We keep hard-bounce suppression workspace-wide because repeatedly attempting a permanently unreachable address through another audience or publication wastes delivery capacity without creating a valid destination. This preserves the hard-bounce boundary described in DOC-004 and later retained in DOC-005. D-20: We limited temporary-failure retries to three attempts within twenty-four hours because unbounded retries would compete with new campaigns and make delivery status difficult to explain. A hard bounce stops further retries immediately.

title: Bounce classification and retry boundaries
text: in DOC-004 and later retained in DOC-005. D-20: We limited temporary-failure retries to three attempts within twenty-four hours because unbounded retries would compete with new campaigns and make delivery status difficult to explain. A hard bounce stops further retries immediately. ## Acceptance and exclusions Duplicate callbacks must not increment retry counts twice. A soft bounce does not mark a subscriber unsubscribed. The activity screen must distinguish a retryable delivery failure from a deliberate preference change. TCK-008 covers worker behavior and the callback deduplication tests. Preference-page wording and recipient opt-out choices belong to DOC-009. Publication-scoped unsubscribe work must not narrow hard-bounce suppression. This specification approves no deployment date and does not imply that TCK-005's later unsubscribe migration has shipped.

title: Unsubscribe receipt copy and preference scope labels
text: # Unsubscribe receipt copy and preference scope labels Owner: Elian Marr. Scope: the confirmation displayed after a recipient changes campaign preferences. This document governs explanatory copy, not transport bounce classification or Pulse administrator onboarding messages. ## Current behavior At this document's date, D-07 in DOC-004 defines unsubscribe suppression as workspace-wide. The confirmation must therefore say that campaign emails from the workspace stop, even when the recipient arrived through one audience's campaign. An audience name may provide context but must not imply audience-limited suppression. ## Decisions D-21: We postponed publication-specific unsubscribe confirmation copy because the approved policy still applies unsubscribe suppression across the workspace. Showing narrower wording before a policy change would misrepresent the effect of the action. D-22: We excluded promotional content from unsubscribe receipts because a confirmation should explain a completed preference change rather than pressure the recipient to return. The page may link to preference management without inserting a campaign offer.

The page may link to preference management without inserting a campaign offer. ## Acceptance and dependencies The confirmation is available without signing into the sender's workspace. It must avoid exposing subscriber custom fields or the full subscriber profile. Repeated visits should explain the effective preference state without reversing it. TCK-009 handles the copy and state assertions. DOC-008 governs hard bounces, which are delivery events rather than preference actions. title: Pricing preview specification for billable subscriber counts
text: # Pricing preview specification for billable subscriber counts Owner: Mira Venn. Scope: an informational pricing estimate for administrators evaluating a Pulse plan. This document does not create a payment system or promise a historical billing adjustment. ## Proposed presentation Show the selected plan, the workspace's current eligible subscriber count, and the timestamp of the estimate. Clearly distinguish audience memberships from unique subscribers so one address in several audiences does not appear to multiply the estimate. Fictional pilot customers described this distinction as more important than a complicated calculator. ## Decisions D-23: We chose a workspace-level deduplicated estimate because counting audience memberships would make the same reachable subscriber appear billable more than once. Suppressed subscribers are excluded from this proposed estimate. D-24: We postponed annual-prepayment checkout because the team has not defined cancellation adjustments and renewal notices. A pricing preview can be evaluated without accepting money under an incomplete billing policy.

It explains its counting basis and avoids implying that it represents delivered messages. No subscriber-level list is downloadable from the preview, preserving the authorization boundary behind D-05. title: Subscriber portability roadmap remains authorization-blocked
text: # Subscriber portability roadmap remains authorization-blocked Owner: Sora Pell. Scope: the roadmap state of subscriber CSV export after requests for migration support. This is distinct from aggregate campaign PDF reports and from inbound CSV imports. ## Current assessment DOC-003 and D-05 postponed subscriber CSV export because field-level access restrictions are not enforced reliably by the proposed read path. A later customer request does not remove that dependency. TCK-003 remains blocked, and TCK-004's aggregate PDF reporting work is not an alternative source of subscriber records. ## Decisions D-25: We continued postponing subscriber CSV export because the authorization prototype still lacks passing negative-permission tests for restricted custom attributes. No delivery date is approved, and no support-operated subscriber download is introduced by this record. D-26: We prioritized a permission-test harness before download formatting because a correctly formatted file is still unsafe if it contains unauthorized fields. The harness must exercise cross-workspace isolation and field omission, not only successful administrator reads.

title: Campaign report scheduling without automatic distribution
text: # Campaign report scheduling without automatic distribution Owner: Fenna Orr. Scope: a proposed reminder to review aggregate campaign results. The proposal does not establish that the PDF attachment in TCK-004 has shipped and does not extend reporting to subscriber-level data. ## Product outline An administrator chooses a campaign and a review date. Pulse creates an in-app reminder linking to the existing report view. The reminder contains a campaign label and timestamp but no subscriber addresses, custom attributes, or recipient-level click history. Aggregate metrics remain subject to report permissions when the user opens the view. ## Decisions D-27: We postponed automatically emailing campaign report attachments because report access can change between scheduling and delivery, and the first scheduler cannot revalidate attachment permissions at send time. The initial proposal is an in-app reminder only. D-28: We chose an explicit reporting timestamp because campaign totals may continue to change after a review reminder is created. A reminder must not imply that its original preview is a permanently final result.

title: Campaign report scheduling without automatic distribution
text: proposal is an in-app reminder only. D-28: We chose an explicit reporting timestamp because campaign totals may continue to change after a review reminder is created. A reminder must not imply that its original preview is a permanently final result. ## Acceptance and limitations Removing report access prevents the reminder from opening protected results. Deleting a campaign cancels pending reminders. The scheduler deduplicates repeated save requests and shows the currently configured review date. TCK-013 records the excluded emailed-attachment shortcut. This work does not replace TCK-004's PDF QA and cannot unblock TCK-003's subscriber export. A future automatic-distribution proposal must explain authorization revalidation before it can supersede D-27. No outbound attachment release is approved here.

title: Sync scheduling update: guarded administrator refresh
text: # Sync scheduling update: guarded administrator refresh Owner: Sora Pell. This record updates recurring inbound synchronization from DOC-007. It does not change the manual CSV import contract in DOC-006 or authorize any subscriber download. ## Evidence and updated scope The connector prototype now serializes work using a per-source lease and tracks the accepted source revision. Administrators in fictional pilot workspaces reported needing a refresh after correcting source records, without waiting for the next nightly run. These are prototype observations, not evidence of production deployment. ## Decisions D-29: We updated D-17 to allow administrator-triggered refresh alongside the nightly batch because the per-source lease now prevents overlapping runs and a deduplication key collapses repeated refresh requests. Nightly processing remains the default; this is a scheduling expansion rather than continuous synchronization. ## Preserved guarantees D-18 remains unchanged: upstream subscription flags cannot clear Pulse suppressions. A manual refresh uses the same revision checks, field permissions, and aggregate status display as a scheduled run. If a run already holds the lease, the interface reports that work is in progress rather than starting a second worker.

title: Sync scheduling update: guarded administrator refresh
text: suppressions. A manual refresh uses the same revision checks, field permissions, and aggregate status display as a scheduled run. title: Preference copy update after publication policy approval
text: # Preference copy update after publication policy approval Owner: Elian Marr. This record updates the copy restriction in DOC-009 after DOC-005 approved publication-scoped unsubscribe handling for new events. TCK-005 still requires rollout evidence; the copy must not get ahead of enabled behavior. ## Decisions D-30: We replaced D-21's blanket postponement of publication-specific confirmation copy with a rollout-gated copy package because D-12 now defines publication scope for new unsubscribe events. The package may name a publication only when the new policy is enabled for that workspace and event. ## State-aware language A new publication opt-out should explain which named sending stream stops. A workspace-wide opt-out must still say that all publications stop. Existing workspace-wide records remain effective under D-13 and must never be displayed as though only one publication were suppressed. Hard bounces remain a separate workspace-wide delivery restriction under D-19. The preference page must not offer a subscription change that claims to make a permanently unreachable address deliverable. D-22's exclusion of promotional content remains unchanged.

title: Preference copy update after publication policy approval
text: only one publication were suppressed. Hard bounces remain a separate workspace-wide delivery restriction under D-19. The preference page must not offer a subscription change that claims to make a permanently unreachable address deliverable. The enablement flag and suppression state jointly select the copy; audience membership is not a substitute for publication identity. title: October roadmap boundaries and release-evidence checklist
text: # October roadmap boundaries and release-evidence checklist Owner: Mira Venn. Scope: consolidate the new workstreams without treating a decision record as evidence of release. This note complements CHAT-005 and preserves the unresolved states described there. ## Decisions D-31: We require a linked verification record before changing a roadmap item to released because approved policy, implementation progress, and customer availability are different claims. A ticket marked ready for QA is not sufficient release evidence. ## Current boundaries Subscriber CSV export remains postponed under D-05 and D-25. The field-permission harness in TCK-012 is a prerequisite, not a download feature. D-14's rejection of a support-operated CSV workaround remains binding, and D-16 still excludes rejected-row download files. Aggregate campaign PDF reporting has no later release confirmation than TCK-004's ready-for-QA state. D-27 excludes automatically emailed report attachments. The in-app review-reminder proposal must not be advertised as a delivered PDF distribution system.

title: Implement behavior-triggered onboarding emails
text: # Implement behavior-triggered onboarding emails Status: In progress Owner: Tavin Reed Related: DOC-001; CHAT-001; CHAT-003 ## Description Implement the three-message administrator sequence from DOC-001. Cancel the import guide when an import succeeds. Enforce the one-message-per-day cross-workspace cap. Never update checklist state from delivery callbacks. At this ticket's date, only verified administrators are eligible under D-02; later policy changes must be applied explicitly. ## Acceptance criteria - A successful import suppresses the pending import guide. - Duplicate worker jobs produce at most one message. - Checklist completion is unchanged after email delivery. ## Comments - 2026-01-26 — Tavin Reed: Added an idempotency key composed of user, workspace, and sequence step. - 2026-01-27 — Mira Venn: D-08: We chose a daily eligibility sweep over exact-time scheduling because the setup guidance is not time-critical and retries are easier to audit. - 2026-01-29 — Elian Marr: Copy now says “continue setup”; it does not promise that reading the email completes a task.

title: Persist onboarding checklist dismissal per user
text: # Persist onboarding checklist dismissal per user Status: Done Owner: Elian Marr Related: DOC-002; CHAT-001 ## Description Persist the setup panel's dismissed state independently for each user. All criteria passed; marking done. This closes the checklist issue, not onboarding-email delivery.

title: Add aggregate campaign report PDF attachment
text: # Add aggregate campaign report PDF attachment Status: Ready for QA Owner: Fenna Orr Related: DOC-003; CHAT-002; CHAT-005 ## Description Generate a PDF containing campaign name, send date, delivered count, opens, clicks, and metric definitions. title: Unsubscribe suppression scope and policy migration

title: Subscriber sync scheduling and manual-refresh update
text: # Subscriber sync scheduling and manual-refresh update Status: in progress ## Description Implement DOC-007's inbound synchronization, preserving D-18. Apply DOC-013's later D-29 scheduling update rather than treating D-17 as permanently nightly-only. ## Comments - Sora Pell (2026-04-03): D-17: Manual refresh is excluded because the worker cannot yet prevent overlapping source runs. Implement nightly batches only. - Tavin Reed (2026-07-24): Prototype lease and request deduplication now serialize source work; regression testing remains incomplete. - Sora Pell (2026-07-29): Reversing the earlier manual-refresh exclusion under D-29 in DOC-013 because the concurrency guard addresses its original reason. Add an administrator refresh control behind the test gate. - Fenna Orr (2026-07-29): This changes the implementation scope, not the deployment state. D-18 still prevents source flags from clearing suppression.

title: Classify hard bounces separately from unsubscribe events
text: # Classify hard bounces separately from unsubscribe events Status: done ## Description Implement D-19 and D-20 from DOC-008: workspace-wide hard-bounce suppression and bounded soft-bounce retries. Never interpret a bounce as a publication preference change. ## Comments - Neri Vale (2026-04-15): Added distinct bounce and unsubscribe event types; the worker stops retries immediately after a hard bounce. - Fenna Orr (2026-04-24): Duplicate callbacks no longer increment the retry counter twice. Three-attempt and twenty-four-hour limits tested. - Neri Vale (2026-05-01): Implementation tests passed; done for this worker change. This does not claim production enablement of the later publication-unsubscribe migration in TCK-005.

title: Unsubscribe confirmation copy with policy-aware variants
text: # Unsubscribe confirmation copy with policy-aware variants Status: in progress ## Description Implement DOC-009's preference confirmation and DOC-014's later gated update. Copy must describe the effective suppression scope and preserve historical workspace-wide opt-outs under D-13. ## Comments - Elian Marr (2026-04-22): Under D-21, publication-specific wording is postponed because the active policy is workspace-wide. Ship no narrow-scope variant yet. - Neri Vale (2026-09-18): DOC-005 approves new-event publication scope but does not prove rollout. Keep old records workspace-wide. - Elian Marr (2026-09-25): Reversing the earlier blanket copy exclusion under D-30 in DOC-014 because publication policy is now approved. Add gated publication wording, never unconditional narrow-scope wording. - Fenna Orr (2026-09-25): Historical opt-out and pre-enablement tests remain pending; status stays in progress.

title: Display deduplicated pricing estimate explanation
text: # Display deduplicated pricing estimate explanation Status: open ## Description Implement the informational estimate from DOC-010 and D-23. Explain unique eligible subscribers versus audience memberships. Do not show an invoice or imply that annual checkout exists. ## Comments - Mira Venn (2026-05-06): Count a repeated address once per workspace; exclude suppressed subscribers from this proposed estimate. - Elian Marr (2026-05-12): Draft copy includes the calculation timestamp and states that this is not a payment demand. - Sora Pell (2026-05-18): Deprioritised because the team must validate suppression-aware counting before exposing a potentially misleading total. Keep open; no estimate is approved for release.

title: Annual-prepayment checkout shortcut
text: # Annual-prepayment checkout shortcut Status: won't do ## Description Request to add an annual purchase button alongside the informational pricing preview. DOC-010 explicitly postpones this scope under D-24. ## Comments - Iona Rell (2026-05-08): A fictional pilot customer asked whether the estimate could lead directly to annual payment. - Mira Venn (2026-05-15): Won't do because cancellation adjustments and renewal notices are undefined; a checkout shortcut would accept money before the policy is ready. D-24 applies. - Sora Pell (2026-05-20): Closed this implementation shortcut, not the long-term possibility of annual plans. TCK-010 remains a separate informational estimate.

title: Field-permission harness for future subscriber downloads
text: # Field-permission harness for future subscriber downloads Status: in progress ## Description Build D-26's negative-permission suite from DOC-011. Cover restricted custom fields and cross-workspace reads before any future subscriber CSV release proposal. TCK-003 remains blocked under D-05 and D-25. ## Comments - Sora Pell (2026-06-23): Add denied-field tests, not only successful administrator fixtures. This is a prerequisite rather than an export endpoint. - Tavin Reed (2026-06-24): Cross-workspace fixtures are implemented; restricted-field omission tests are still failing. - Mira Venn (2026-06-25): Do not assign an export release date from this ticket's progress. D-25 continues the postponement until the review gate is met.

title: Automatically email campaign PDF attachments
text: # Automatically email campaign PDF attachments Status: won't do ## Description Request to attach aggregate campaign reports to scheduled outbound review emails. This is not subscriber CSV export, but DOC-012 excludes automatic distribution under D-27. ## Comments - Fenna Orr (2026-07-07): The in-app review reminder can link to an access-checked report view; it need not send an attachment. - Sora Pell (2026-07-09): Won't do because the scheduler cannot revalidate report permissions at attachment-send time. D-27 explicitly postpones that capability. - Mira Venn (2026-07-10): Closing the shortcut. TCK-004 still has no release evidence beyond ready for QA; this ticket does not imply PDF availability.

title: Recover expired subscriber-sync leases safely
text: # Recover expired subscriber-sync leases safely Status: open ## Description Test lease-expiry recovery required by D-29 in DOC-013. A refresh request must not launch a second writer while a valid source lease is held. Preserve DOC-007's revision ordering and D-18 suppression authority. ## Comments - Tavin Reed (2026-07-29): Added a case where the original worker resumes after its lease expires; the stale lease token must fail the commit check. - Fenna Orr (2026-08-03): Need a crash-between-read-and-commit fixture before we can approve the refresh control. - Sora Pell (2026-08-05): Keep open. Policy approval for manual refresh is not evidence of concurrency correctness or production rollout.

title: Require evidence before roadmap release-state changes
text: # Require evidence before roadmap release-state changes Status: done ## Description Add a roadmap review template implementing D-31 in DOC-015. Require a verification result, enabled scope, and verification date before an item can be labelled released. This template does not change feature statuses by itself. ## Comments - Mira Venn (2026-10-14): Added separate fields for policy approval, implementation state, and customer availability. - Iona Rell (2026-10-15): Included examples distinguishing subscriber CSV export, aggregate PDF reporting, and publication preference copy. - Elian Marr (2026-10-16): Template reviewed and published internally; this documentation task is done. TCK-003 remains blocked and TCK-005 has no new rollout confirmation.

title: Activation triage: email delivery is not checklist progress
text: # Activation triage: email delivery is not checklist progress Channel: #activation-lab Thread date: 2026-02-06 - 09:10 — Iona Rell: Fictional pilot customer Junia Kest from Lantern Finch says the welcome email arrived, but the setup panel still asks her to import an audience. - 09:12 — Elian Marr: That is expected unless an import succeeded. DOC-002 measures actual setup actions, not email receipt. - 09:14 — Tavin Reed: TCK-001 controls the email sequence. TCK-002 controls checklist visibility. They share events but not completion rules. - 09:17 — Mira Venn: D-10: We kept email engagement out of checklist completion because opening instructions does not demonstrate successful setup. - 09:20 — Iona Rell: Junia confirmed she only read the guide. I will explain the remaining import step rather than file a progress bug. - 09:23 — Elian Marr: TCK-002 is done, but that only establishes per-user dismissal and action-derived completion. It says nothing about the email worker's release state.

title: Customer asks for campaign results, not subscriber records
text: # Customer asks for campaign results, not subscriber records Channel: #customer-notes Thread date: 2026-02-18 - 14:02 — Iona Rell: Fictional customer Oren Ves from Copper Moth asked for an “export” before a monthly review. I asked which information he needs. - 14:05 — Iona Rell: He wants delivered totals, open estimates, and click counts in an attachment. He explicitly does not need subscriber addresses. - 14:07 — Mira Venn: That is the aggregate campaign report in DOC-003, not the subscriber CSV feature postponed by D-05. - 14:10 — Sora Pell: Correct. The blocked subscriber-field read path is irrelevant only while the report stays aggregate and enforces report permissions. - 14:12 — Fenna Orr: I will draft TCK-004 around a PDF. No recipient-level appendix. - 14:15 — Mira Venn: Keep the roadmap labels precise. “Exports are coming” would incorrectly promise subscriber downloads.

title: Decision update: onboarding emails for invited campaign editors
text: # Decision update: onboarding emails for invited campaign editors Channel: #activation-lab Thread date: 2026-06-11 - 10:00 — Mira Venn: Reviewing D-02 from DOC-001. Verified administrators were the only onboarding-email recipients in the initial scope. - 10:03 — Iona Rell: Fictional pilot editor Zelin Ash from Paper Heron can create drafts but receives no introduction after accepting an invitation. Three pilot interviews reported the same role mismatch. - 10:06 — Mira Venn: D-11: We expanded onboarding-email eligibility to verified invited campaign editors because their permissions now allow draft creation and the administrator-only flow leaves that supported action unexplained. This supersedes D-02's administrator-only restriction. - 10:09 — Tavin Reed: Editors will receive welcome and draft-building guidance only. Import and domain-verification prompts remain restricted to administrators. - 10:12 — Elian Marr: This changes message eligibility, not checklist permissions or shared task state. DOC-002 remains the checklist contract. - 10:15 — Mira Venn: Approved as policy today; implementation is pending an explicit update to TCK-001. Keep the cross-workspace daily cap and behavior-based suppression from D-01.

title: Publication unsubscribe feedback challenges workspace-wide policy
text: # Publication unsubscribe feedback challenges workspace-wide policy Channel: #deliverability-review Thread date: 2026-08-24 - 11:01 — Iona Rell: Fictional customer Aven Dorr from Velvet Acorn runs two named publications in one workspace. A reader left the weekly digest and unintentionally stopped product notes too. - 11:04 — Neri Vale: That matches D-07 in DOC-004. Unsubscribe suppression is currently workspace-wide, even across distinct audiences. - 11:07 — Mira Venn: Their publication identities are distinct. We should review the policy, but this conversation does not approve a new scope. - 11:11 — Fenna Orr: An audience is a recipient collection; a publication is a recognizable sending stream. We cannot substitute an audience identifier and call the problem solved. - 11:14 — Neri Vale: Any proposal must preserve historical workspace-wide opt-outs and keep hard-bounce suppression separate. - 11:18 — Mira Venn: I will request a replacement decision record. Until then, TCK-005 must continue to test the existing contract. The eventual approved update belongs in DOC-005.

title: October roadmap check: CSV still postponed; PDF not portability

title: October roadmap check: CSV still postponed; PDF not portability
text: # October roadmap check: CSV still postponed; PDF not portability Channel: #roadmap-review Thread date: 2026-10-09 - 15:00 — Iona Rell: Fictional customer Junia Kest from Lantern Finch now needs subscriber records for an internal migration. A campaign-results PDF will not meet that request. - 15:03 — Sora Pell: Subscriber CSV export remains postponed under D-05. TCK-003 is still blocked; we have no approved release date or supported download endpoint. - 15:06 — Fenna Orr: TCK-004's last recorded state is ready for QA. This corpus contains no later confirmation that aggregate PDF reports shipped. - 15:09 — Mira Venn: D-14: We rejected a support-operated manual CSV workaround because it would bypass the same field-authorization boundary blocking the product feature. - 15:12 — Iona Rell: I will explain the limitation without promising timing. Her migration request is subscriber portability, not aggregate analytics. - 15:15 — Neri Vale: DOC-005 updated unsubscribe scope, but that policy approval did not fix CSV authorization. TCK-005 is also still awaiting rollout evidence. - 15:18 — Mira Venn: Correct. Keep those decisions independent in the roadmap: permission-safe subscriber download, aggregate campaign reporting, and publication unsubscribe scope.

title: Customer feedback: setup email versus completed setup
text: # Customer feedback: setup email versus completed setup Channel: #customer-notes Iona Rell (09:00): Fictional customer Luma Serr from Willow Prism says the welcome email made her expect the import checklist task to be complete. Elian Marr (09:03): DOC-002 and D-10 require a successful action. Reading or receiving setup guidance cannot complete the task. Iona Rell (09:06): She wants the email button to say what remains, not just “continue.” Her audience file is still only a preview. Tavin Reed (09:09): DOC-006 makes preview and commit separate. TCK-006 emits completion only after commit. Mira Venn (09:12): Keep that boundary because a preview can still fail or be cancelled. Clarify the button copy without changing progress semantics. Iona Rell (09:15): I will relay that distinction. No new checklist behavior or email-recipient expansion is being promised.

title: Internal import review: error summary is not a download
text: # Internal import review: error summary is not a download Channel: #import-design Tavin Reed (10:00): Can we attach a rejected-row CSV to the preview? It would make cleanup convenient. Sora Pell (10:03): D-16 in DOC-006 postpones that because custom attributes could escape through a second download path before authorization is sound. Elian Marr (10:06): An authenticated summary can show row numbers and validation categories without building that endpoint. Mira Venn (10:09): Keep the on-screen summary because it supports correction without bypassing the postponed download boundary. Do not reinterpret D-15 partial acceptance as approval for rejection files. Tavin Reed (10:12): TCK-006 will include summary tests only. Subscriber CSV export remains a separate postponed feature under D-05.

title: Customer feedback: repaired source data needs a fresh sync
text: # Customer feedback: repaired source data needs a fresh sync Channel: #customer-notes Iona Rell (13:00): Fictional customer Rovin Eska from Amber Loom corrected source attributes at noon and asked why Pulse would wait until night. Sora Pell (13:03): D-17 chose nightly runs because the initial worker lacked a per-source concurrency guard. DOC-007 states that reason explicitly. Iona Rell (13:06): He wants a refresh button, not another CSV upload. His source has revision identifiers. Tavin Reed (13:09): That belongs to subscriber sync, not DOC-006's one-time audience import. We can test a lease and duplicate-request key. Mira Venn (13:12): Gather concurrency evidence before updating policy because a fast refresh that overwrites newer data would be worse than a clear wait. Iona Rell (13:15): I will describe it as a request under review, not an available feature.

title: Customer feedback: repeated audience memberships confuse pricing
text: # Customer feedback: repeated audience memberships confuse pricing Channel: #customer-notes Iona Rell (11:00): Fictional customer Tessa Vonn from Moss Lantern has the same subscribers in several audiences and fears being charged once per membership. Mira Venn (11:03): D-23 in DOC-010 proposes deduplicated workspace-level eligible subscribers, not membership counts. Elian Marr (11:06): The preview should explain the basis in plain language and show its timestamp. It must not resemble an invoice. Iona Rell (11:09): She also asked for annual checkout, but understands the counting question comes first. Mira Venn (11:12): D-24 postpones checkout because cancellation adjustments and renewal notices are undefined. Do not turn interest into a payment promise. Sora Pell (11:15): TCK-010 covers the estimate; TCK-011 covers the excluded purchase shortcut. Neither is a billing-system release.

title: Customer feedback: migration requires subscriber export
text: # Customer feedback: migration requires subscriber export Channel: #customer-notes Iona Rell (14:00): Fictional customer Daren Pellis from Silver Sprig needs subscriber records for a migration, not a campaign chart attachment. Sora Pell (14:03): DOC-011 and D-25 continue the subscriber CSV postponement because restricted-field negative tests still fail. Iona Rell (14:06): Could support run a one-off script instead? The customer asked whether that avoids the product delay. Mira Venn (14:09): No workaround is approved here. The same field-authorization boundary would apply to a support-run download. Tavin Reed (14:12): TCK-012 builds the permission harness. It is not an endpoint or a migration service. Iona Rell (14:15): I will state the limitation without a release date. TCK-004's aggregate PDF cannot satisfy this portability request.

title: Customer feedback: bounce warning mistaken for unsubscribe
text: # Customer feedback: bounce warning mistaken for unsubscribe Channel: #customer-notes Iona Rell (15:00): Fictional customer Neva Orrel from Satin Grove thought a hard-bounce badge meant the recipient clicked unsubscribe. Neri Vale (15:03): DOC-008 separates transport failure from preference changes. D-19 keeps a permanently unreachable address suppressed workspace-wide. Elian Marr (15:06): DOC-009's unsubscribe receipt is for deliberate preference actions. We should not reuse that label for bounces. Iona Rell (15:09): The customer asked whether moving the address to another audience would clear it. Neri Vale (15:12): It must not, because another audience does not repair the destination. TCK-008 tests the workspace-wide boundary. Elian Marr (15:15): I will keep the status explanations distinct; no change to unsubscribe scope is approved in this discussion.

title: Internal sync decision: permit guarded manual refresh
text: # Internal sync decision: permit guarded manual refresh Channel: #sync-workers Tavin Reed (10:00): The prototype now takes a per-source lease and deduplicates repeated refresh requests. Nightly work uses the same path. Sora Pell (10:03): D-17 originally excluded manual refresh because overlapping runs were unsafe. That original reason is now addressed in the prototype design. Mira Venn (10:06): Reverse the nightly-only restriction in policy under D-29, recorded today in DOC-013, because the concurrency guard supports serialized refresh requests. Keep nightly batches as the default. Fenna Orr (10:09): Approval still needs crash and lease-expiry tests before rollout. A prototype observation is not production evidence. Tavin Reed (10:12): TCK-007 will adopt the revised scope tomorrow; TCK-014 will track recovery tests. Sora Pell (10:15): D-18 is unchanged. Refresh can update permitted fields but must never clear a Pulse suppression.

title: Internal delivery review: do not merge bounce and opt-out states
text: # Internal delivery review: do not merge bounce and opt-out states Channel: #deliverability-review Elian Marr (09:00): Could a single “inactive” badge cover hard bounces and unsubscribes to simplify the audience table? Neri Vale (09:03): That would hide why sending stopped. DOC-008 and D-19 treat a hard bounce as a delivery failure, not a recipient preference. Mira Venn (09:06): Keep separate labels because support needs to explain different causes and cannot suggest a preference change fixes an unreachable address. Fenna Orr (09:09): TCK-008 already tests distinct event types. Merging display state would undermine those explanations. Elian Marr (09:12): I withdraw the combined-label proposal. Publication unsubscribe scope still follows DOC-004 at this date; no later policy approval is implied.

title: Internal reporting review: reminder is not emailed attachment
text: # Internal reporting review: reminder is not emailed attachment Channel: #reporting-design Fenna Orr (16:00): The review reminder could attach a cached campaign PDF. Should we reuse the scheduler's stored access result? Sora Pell (16:03): No. Access might change before delivery, and the scheduler cannot revalidate attachment permissions. D-27 in DOC-012 postpones that path. Mira Venn (16:06): Reject the attachment shortcut because a prior permission check is not proof of current access. Keep the in-app reminder proposal only. Elian Marr (16:09): Opening its link will check report access at that time. The reminder itself contains no subscriber data. Fenna Orr (16:12): TCK-013 will close the shortcut. This also does not prove that TCK-004's PDF work has shipped.

title: Internal copy review: publication wording must follow rollout
text: # Internal copy review: publication wording must follow rollout Channel: #preference-copy Elian Marr (11:00): DOC-005 approves publication scope, so can we replace every unsubscribe confirmation with the publication name? Neri Vale (11:03): No. D-13 preserves historical workspace-wide records, and TCK-005 has no rollout confirmation. Narrow wording would misstate those opt-outs. Mira Venn (11:06): D-30 in DOC-014 updates D-21 only to permit gated copy because the new policy is approved, not universally active. Fenna Orr (11:09): Tests need both an old workspace-wide record and a new publication opt-out, plus the disabled-rollout case. Elian Marr (11:12): TCK-009 will select wording from effective state and enablement. Audience membership alone cannot determine scope. Neri Vale (11:15): Keep hard bounces separate under D-19 and keep promotional content out under D-22. Neither boundary changed today.
